To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have predicted the protein kinases that phosphorylate the yeast phosphoprotein dataset.

protein kinase substrates have been assigned to the majority of the yeast phosphoprotein sites identified by mass spectrometry, with the predictions being based on the substrate specificity of the protein kinase and on the sequence of the phosphorylated peptide.

we have predicted which protein kinases are responsible for the phosphorylating the phosphoproteomics data in yeast, that these predictions can be used to link kinases and phosphosites, and that the predictions can be used as a tool to assign functions to uncharacterized proteins in the yeast phosphoprotome.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how phosphorylation is used as a regulatory mechanism in yeast and how this knowledge can be exploited to understand phosphorylation in other species.
the identification of the protein kinome and phosphoproteome and the establishment of links between them.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Predikin is an excellent tool for the prediction of protein kinases that can phosphorylate specific phosphopeptides.
the protein kinase phosphoprotein network is a complex web, with many nodes and many edges, which is not fully understood.
the protein kinases that are represented in our dataset are likely to have a general cellular role in yeast.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a large number of protein kinase-phosphoprotein interactions that can be experimentally verified.
we have predicted the phosphorylation sites for 116 yeast protein kinases on 216 phosphoproteins, which are involved in various cellular processes.

we have used a bioinformatic tool to predict protein kinase substrates in yeast and have found that the predictions are useful for establishing links between phosphoproteins, protein kinases and biological functions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the phosphoprotein kinases in yeast have housekeeping functions and are not specific to particular cellular responses.
Predikin can be used to make testable predictions about the kinase-phosphoprotein links.
protein kinase substrate predictions can be used to generate testable hypotheses for further study of the phosphoproteomic data.
